On a single contrast-enhanced phase, a renal lesion between about 20 and 70 HU is “indeterminate”: it may be a cyst with proteinaceous or hemorrhagic content (which does not enhance) or a poorly vascularized solid or complex cystic lesion. The difference is made by comparison with the unenhanced phase (an increase of at least 20 HU = enhancement) or by subtraction MRI.
Bosniak 2019: simple cysts (I) and minimally complex cystic lesions (II) require no follow-up; IIF follow-up; III-IV cystic lesions with thick septa or walls that enhance, or nodules: increasing risk of malignancy.
Mixed epithelial and stromal tumor (MEST) is a rare benign tumor, more frequent in middle-aged women, usually cystic-solid; on imaging it cannot be distinguished from cystic renal carcinoma, and for this reason it is often resected.
Lesione renale tra 20 e 70 HU in una sol: Renal lesion between 20 and 70 HU on a single phase: indeterminate; do not call it a cyst or a tumor without the unenhanced phase or MRI.
Nefrectomia radicale: tumore misto epite: Radical nephrectomy: mixed epithelial and stromal tumor (MEST), benign, 4.5 cm (C4KC-KiTS collection clinical data).
